details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reportedly launched missile and drone attacks on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain on July 8, in retaliation for prior American airstrikes on Iranian territory. This escalation follows the unofficial end of a ceasefire and renewed tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. Bitcoin briefly dropped below $100,000 following the news but quickly recovered.
title: US-Iran Hostilities Escalate, Bitcoin Whipsaws Near $100K

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has revised down its 2026 global growth forecast for the second time this year, citing the "lingering effects" of the energy shock from the US-Iran conflict. Global growth is now projected at 3.0%, a modest slowdown partly offset by accelerated demand-driven momentum in the global technology cycle, particularly due to advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI).
title: IMF Cuts 2026 Global Growth Forecast Amid Iran War, AI Offers Partial Offset

details: A Wall Street Journal analysis suggests that rising geopolitical tensions, persistent inflation, and more frequent economic shocks are compelling investors to overhaul traditional portfolio strategies. Conflicts in the Middle East and other global instabilities are making inflationary shocks more common and are expected to increase volatility across asset classes.
title: Geopolitical Risks Force Rethink of Investment Strategies

details: Bitcoin and Ether Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) have snapped an eight-week streak of outflows, recording a combined inflow of $282 million. This indicates renewed institutional interest and a shift in sentiment for these major cryptocurrencies.
title: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs Reverse Outflow Trend with Significant Inflows

details: A recent analysis by The Wall Street Journal, highlighted by the Bank Policy Institute, reveals that nations targeted by US sanctions, including Iran, Russia, and North Korea, have "dramatically increased" their use of cryptocurrency to circumvent restrictions. This activity, involving an estimated $100 billion in digital assets last year, is used for purposes like paying smugglers and acquiring weapons.
title: Iran and Other Rogue Nations Increase Crypto Use to Evade Sanctions
